metadata.original_issue: Segfault when applying max_pool1d to non-contiguous 3D tensor

knowledge_abstraction.general_principle: Operators may fail when tensor storage is non-contiguous because underlying kernel or backend implementations may assume contiguous memory access patterns and not correctly handle arbitrary strides.

risk_dimensions.shape: Tensors with dims greater than 2 where permutation, transpose, or slicing changes the memory layout
risk_dimensions.memory: Non-contiguous tensor storage produced by layout-changing operations such as permute, transpose, or slicing
risk_dimensions.device: CPU and GPU devices may exhibit different memory layout handling behavior

failure_mechanism.description: Pooling kernels may assume contiguous input memory or compute access indices without fully accounting for non-contiguous strides, leading to out-of-bounds access or segmentation faults.

input_exploration: Explore non-contiguous tensors produced by permute, transpose, or slicing operations
Vary input dimensionality and shape combinations, especially 3D and higher
Include small or degenerate spatial dimensions with non-contiguous layouts
constraint_awareness: Track tensor contiguity and stride information before invoking operators
Consider pooling parameters including kernel_size, stride, padding, and especially kernel_size=1
oracle_strategy: Monitor for crashes, segmentation faults, or abnormal process termination
Compare outputs and completion behavior against a contiguous reference baseline

transferability.reason: Memory layout assumptions are common across tensor operators that delegate to kernels or backend libraries, so non-contiguous layout risks can affect many APIs beyond max_pool1d.

important_considerations: Generate inputs with non-contiguous memory layouts
Combine layout permutations with varied pooling parameters
Test both CPU and GPU execution paths
generation_strategy: Create contiguous base tensors, apply layout-changing operations such as permute, transpose, or slicing, then invoke the operator under test while monitoring process stability and comparing results against contiguous baselines.
